questions.question: Which scientist first saw and described a live cell?

solution.key_concept: Historical milestones in the discovery of the cell.
steps: Anton von Leeuwenhoek was the first to see and describe a live cell.
Robert Brown later discovered the nucleus.
Schleiden and Virchow made later contributions to cell theory.
solution.why_not_others: Robert Brown discovered the nucleus. Schleiden studied plant cells and co-proposed cell theory. Virchow proposed Omnis cellula-e cellula.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the discoverer of the nucleus (Robert Brown) with the first observer of a live cell.

questions.question: The cell theory proposed by Schleiden and Schwann was incomplete. Which aspect did it fail to explain, which Rudolf Virchow later supplied?
options: That all plants are composed of different kinds of cells
That animal cells have a thin outer layer, the plasma membrane
That the cell wall is unique to plant cells

steps: Schleiden and Schwann's cell theory did not explain how new cells form.
In 1855 Virchow stated that new cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).
His addition completed the theory.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): How new cells are formed
solution.why_not_others: Options 1-3 were observations made by Schleiden and Schwann themselves, so they were already part of the original theory.
solution.common_trap: Picking one of Schleiden's or Schwann's own observations as the missing part.

questions.question: Which of the following was reported by Theodore Schwann?
options: Cells have a thin outer layer, now called the plasma membrane, and the cell wall is unique to plant cells
All plants are made of different kinds of cells that form tissues
New cells arise from pre-existing cells

solution.key_concept: Matching scientists to their contributions to cell biology.
steps: Schwann (1839) studied animal cells.
He reported a thin outer layer (the plasma membrane) in animal cells.
He also concluded that the cell wall is unique to plant cells.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Cells have a thin outer layer, now called the plasma membrane, and the cell wall is unique to plant cells
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 is Schleiden's observation (1838). Option 3 is Virchow's (1855). The nucleus was discovered by Robert Brown.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up Schleiden (plants) with Schwann (animals).

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: The cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of life, and anything less than a complete cell cannot live independently.
statements.R: The cell theory of Schleiden and Schwann explained that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Scope of the original cell theory versus Virchow's contribution.
steps: The cell is the basic unit of life, and less than a complete cell cannot live independently. A is true.
Schleiden and Schwann's theory did not explain how new cells form.
That idea came from Virchow in 1855, so R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options 1, 2 and 4 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Crediting Omnis cellula-e cellula to Schleiden and Schwann instead of Virchow.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Schleiden's observations (1838) were made on plants, whereas Schwann's (1839) were made on animal cells.
statements.II: Modern cell theory states that all living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells, and that all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Chronology of cell theory and the two tenets of modern cell theory.
steps: Schleiden, a botanist, worked on plants in 1838. Schwann, a zoologist, worked on animal cells in 1839. Statement I is correct.
Modern cell theory has two tenets: organisms are made of cells and products of cells, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells. Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the facts, so any option marking either one as incorrect is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the years or the organisms studied by Schleiden and Schwann, or forgetting 'products of cells'.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is a eukaryote?

steps: Prokaryotes are bacteria, cyanobacteria, mycoplasma and PPLO.
Eukaryotes include protists, fungi, plants and animals.
So a fungus is the eukaryote.
solution.why_not_others: Mycoplasma, cyanobacteria and PPLO all lack a membrane-bound nucleus, so they are prokaryotes.
solution.common_trap: Calling fungi prokaryotes because they are microscopic or simple.

questions.question: A prokaryotic ribosome is made of a 50S and a 30S subunit. What is the sedimentation coefficient of the complete ribosome?

steps: The S value depends on sedimentation rate, which depends on size and shape.
So subunit S values cannot simply be added together.
The prokaryotic ribosome (50S + 30S) is 70S.
solution.why_not_others: 80S comes from adding the S values, and it is also the eukaryotic ribosome. 20S comes from subtracting them. 60S is a eukaryotic large subunit.
solution.common_trap: Adding 50S and 30S to get 80S.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a cell with its approximate size?

steps: Mycoplasma is the smallest cell, about $0.3\ \mu m$.
Bacteria are 3 to $5\ \mu m$.
A human RBC is about $7\ \mu m$.
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 2 swap the RBC and Mycoplasma sizes. Bacteria are 3 to $5\ \mu m$, not $0.3\ \mu m$.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the sizes of Mycoplasma and the human RBC.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

steps: Bacillus is rod-shaped (A-III).
Coccus is spherical (B-I).
Vibrio is comma-shaped (C-II).
Spirillum is spiral (D-IV).
solution.why_not_others: The other options swap bacillus with coccus, or vibrio with spirillum.
solution.common_trap: Confusing vibrio (comma) with spirillum (spiral).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are correct?

statements.A: Plasmids are small circular extrachromosomal DNA that may confer antibiotic resistance.
statements.B: Eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S, made of 60S and 40S subunits.
statements.C: Prokaryotic cells possess mitochondria but lack endoplasmic reticulum.
statements.D: A polysome consists of several ribosomes attached to a single mRNA.
statements.E: Nerve cells are the largest isolated single cells.

options: A, B, C and D only

solution.key_concept: Features of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
steps: A is correct: plasmids are extrachromosomal and may confer antibiotic resistance.
B is correct: eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S (60S + 40S).
C is wrong: prokaryotes have no membrane-bound organelles, so they have no mitochondria.
D is correct: several ribosomes on one mRNA form a polysome.
E is wrong: nerve cells are the longest cells, while the ostrich egg is the largest isolated single cell.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 leaves out D. Option 2 includes C. Option 4 includes E and leaves out A.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the longest cell (nerve cell) with the largest isolated cell (ostrich egg).

questions.question: The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane was proposed by

steps: Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model in 1972.
It describes a quasi-fluid lipid bilayer that allows lateral movement of proteins.
solution.why_not_others: Schleiden and Schwann proposed cell theory. Camillo Golgi observed the Golgi apparatus. Virchow proposed Omnis cellula-e cellula.
solution.common_trap: Linking the plasma membrane to Schwann, who only described it in animal cells.

questions.question: The middle lamella that holds neighbouring plant cells together is mainly composed of

solution.key_concept: Composition of the plant cell wall layers.
steps: The middle lamella is mainly calcium pectate.
Cellulose and hemicellulose are components of the plant cell wall proper.
Calcium carbonate occurs in algal walls.
solution.why_not_others: Cellulose and hemicellulose belong to the primary and secondary walls. Calcium carbonate is found in algal cell walls.
solution.common_trap: Choosing cellulose because it is the best-known wall component.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the bacterial mesosome?
options: DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells

steps: The mesosome is an extension of the plasma membrane into the cell.
It helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution, respiration and secretion, and it increases membrane surface area.
Motility is the role of flagella, not mesosomes.
solution.why_not_others: Options 1-3 are all listed functions of the mesosome.
solution.common_trap: Thinking every membrane extension also helps the cell move.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Pili and fimbriae are the structures responsible for motility in bacteria.
statements.R: A bacterial flagellum is composed of three parts: filament, hook and basal body.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

steps: Pili and fimbriae help attachment, not motility, so A is false.
Bacteria move by flagella, which have a filament, a hook and a basal body, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every bacterial surface appendage helps in movement.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In the human RBC membrane, protein (about 52%) is present in a greater proportion than lipid (about 40%).
statements.II: The secondary wall of a plant cell is formed on the outer side of the primary wall.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Membrane composition and cell wall layering.
steps: The human RBC membrane has about 52% protein and 40% lipid, so Statement I is correct.
The secondary wall forms on the inner side of the primary wall, towards the membrane, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II reverses the position of the secondary wall, so options 1 and 4 fail. Statement I is true, so options 2 and 4 fail.
solution.common_trap: Assuming lipid exceeds protein in the membrane, or placing the secondary wall outside the primary wall.

questions.question: The membrane that bounds the vacuole in a plant cell is called the

steps: The vacuole is bounded by a single membrane called the tonoplast.
The tonoplast transports ions into the vacuole against the concentration gradient.
solution.why_not_others: The plasma membrane bounds the whole cell. The middle lamella cements adjacent cell walls. Cisternae are the flat sacs of the Golgi.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the tonoplast with the plasma membrane.

questions.question: In animal cells, steroidal hormones are synthesised in the

steps: Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and is the major site of lipid synthesis.
In animal cells, steroidal hormones are lipid-derived and are made in the SER.
solution.why_not_others: RER makes proteins for secretion. The Golgi packages materials and forms glycoproteins. Lysosomes carry out hydrolytic digestion.
solution.common_trap: Choosing RER because hormones are associated with secretion.

questions.question: Which of the following organelles is a part of the endomembrane system?

steps: The endomembrane system comprises the ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles, whose functions are coordinated.
Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not included.
solution.why_not_others: The mitochondrion, peroxisome and chloroplast are membrane-bound, but their functions are not coordinated with the ER and Golgi.
solution.common_trap: Including every membrane-bound organelle in the endomembrane system.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

steps: The cis (forming) face of the Golgi receives material from the ER (A-II).
Lysosomes contain acid hydrolases (B-III).
The contractile vacuole of Amoeba carries out osmoregulation and excretion (C-I).
RER is involved in protein synthesis and secretion (D-IV).
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps A and B. Option 2 swaps C and D. Option 4 swaps A and D.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the receiving role of the cis face with the protein-synthesising role of the RER.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and vacuoles are correct?

statements.A: The Golgi apparatus is the site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.
statements.B: The tonoplast transports ions into the vacuole against the concentration gradient, so the concentration of vacuolar sap exceeds that of the cytoplasm.
statements.C: The trans face of the Golgi is the convex forming face.
statements.D: Lysosomes bud off from the Golgi and contain hydrolases that are optimally active at acidic pH.

solution.key_concept: Structure and function of the Golgi, lysosomes and vacuoles.
steps: A is correct: glycoproteins and glycolipids are formed in the Golgi.
B is correct: the tonoplast pumps ions in against the gradient, which concentrates the sap.
C is wrong: the cis face is the convex forming face, while the trans face is the concave maturing face.
D is correct: lysosomes come from the Golgi and contain acid hydrolases.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 2 and 3 include the false statement C. Option 4 leaves out the true statement B.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the cis (convex, forming) and trans (concave, maturing) faces of the Golgi.
